title: Hymns to John the Baptist and John the Apostle ask cleansing, healing, and vision of the Word
source_text: LIV. Similiter his verbis incipit Hymnus quidam de Johanne Baptista, Baptista Christi inclyte, Qui Christum prodis indice, Nos miserando respice, Culpas solve nostras, Ablue. Et in alio Hymno ad eundem dicitur, Solve polluti labii reatum Sancte Johannes. Ad Joannem autem Apostolum haec habetur oratio: Te rogamus, te precamur, Sancte Dei Apostole, Tolle pestem, aufer ulcus, & foveto languidos: Pelle morbum, cede hostem, & remove scandalum. Et in alio Hymno Eidem Joanni dicitur, Te promis alme cordibus, Caeli senator poscimus: Da Verbi vultum cernere, Qui Verbum doces credere.
pass_a_gloss: Likewise a certain Hymn concerning John the Baptist begins with these words: Illustrious Baptist of Christ, Who goest before Christ as pointer, Look on us with pity, Loose our faults, Wash them away. And in another Hymn to the same it is said, Loose the guilt of polluted lip, Saint John. But to John the Apostle this prayer is had: We ask Thee, we pray Thee, Holy Apostle of God, Take away the plague, remove the ulcer, and cherish the languishing: Drive out disease, yield the enemy, and remove scandal. And in another Hymn to the same John it is said: We ask Thee, kind one, promised to hearts, Senator of heaven: Grant to discern the face of the Word, Who teachest to believe the Word.
pass_b_english: Baptist hymns beg pity, loosing of faults, and cleansing of polluted lips.
Apostle John is asked to lift plague and scandal and grant sight of the Word’s face.

lemmas.gloss: grant to discern the face of the Word

choices.why: Opens the cited Baptist hymn as public-cult evidence.
